questions.prompt: Which four evaluation semantics are defined for P2900 contract assertions in C++26?
options: ignore, observe, enforce, and quick_enforce
debug, release, audit, and assume
off, warn, throw_on_fail, and abort
constexpr_only, runtime_check, log, and trap
questions.explanation: P2900 defines four evaluation semantics: ignore (compile-checked, not evaluated at runtime), observe (evaluate and invoke handler, then continue), enforce (evaluate, invoke handler, then terminate), and quick_enforce (evaluate and terminate immediately without calling the handler).

questions.prompt: In P2996 static reflection, what is the type of the expression ^^MyStruct, and when can it exist?
questions.code:
struct MyStruct { int x; };
constexpr auto r = ^^MyStruct;
options: std::type_info, usable at runtime
std::meta::info, a consteval-only scalar type usable strictly in constant evaluation
std::string_view containing "MyStruct"
std::tuple<int> describing its members
questions.explanation: The reflection operator ^^ yields a value of std::meta::info, which is a consteval-only type in [expr.reflect] and [meta.reflection]. It cannot persist as a runtime object or be stored outside constant evaluation.

questions.prompt: Why does GCC 16 (-std=c++26 -fcontracts) reject the following P2900 postcondition?
options: post cannot refer to two parameters in the same expression
a and b are integer types rather than references
Any non-reference parameter referenced inside a postcondition specifier must be declared const
post must appear before pre on the declaration
questions.explanation: Under P2900 [dcl.contract.func], if a postcondition names a by-value parameter of the function, that parameter must be const-qualified on the definition (e.g., const int a, const int b); otherwise the function could mutate its local copy and make the postcondition ambiguous.

questions.prompt: In P2300 std::execution, what work runs when you evaluate only the pipeline expression auto s = std::execution::just(10) | std::execution::then(fn);?
questions.code:
auto s = std::execution::just(10)
       | std::execution::then([](int x) { side_effect(); return x + 1; });
options: side_effect() runs eagerly on the calling thread
side_effect() is queued on the default system thread pool immediately
Nothing executes yet: senders are lazy descriptions that do not run until connected to a receiver and started (or consumed by std::this_thread::sync_wait)
Compilation fails because just() cannot precede then()
questions.explanation: P2300 senders are lazy work descriptions. Constructing and piping senders builds a typed expression graph without starting execution or allocating work until connect(sender, receiver) produces an operation state and start(op) (or sync_wait) runs it.

questions.prompt: Under C++26 P2795 (Erroneous Behavior), what happens at runtime when a program reads an uninitialized local int x; without [[indeterminate]]?
options: Unbounded undefined behavior, allowing compilers to eliminate surrounding checks
Ill-formed diagnostic required: the program fails to compile
Throws std::logic_error at runtime
Erroneous behavior: the program contains a bug, yet runtime execution is well-defined because x receives an implementation-determined erroneous value rather than causing UB
questions.explanation: P2795 [basic.indet] classifies reading an uninitialized automatic variable (not marked [[indeterminate]]) as erroneous behavior rather than undefined behavior. Implementations initialize it to an erroneous value (such as zero or a fixed pattern), eliminating UB time-travel optimizations.

questions.prompt: What are the exact three completion channels a P2300 receiver handles in std::execution?
options: set_value, set_error, and set_stopped
on_next, on_error, and on_complete
resolve, reject, and finally
return_value, throw_exception, and cancel_token
questions.explanation: In [exec.recv], every P2300 sender completes by invoking exactly one of three receiver customization points: set_value(rcvr, args...), set_error(rcvr, err), or set_stopped(rcvr) (representing cooperative cancellation).
